hints: Focus on what changes as you move down Group 2 from magnesium to barium, with more proton shells being added.
Think about how extra inner electron shells affect both the size of the $\text{M}^{2+}$ ion and the shielding felt by the outer electrons.
Recall the solubility trend for Group 2 hydroxides and connect all three statements to decide which combination fits.
walkthrough:
**Set the direction down Group 2**

Think of going Mg to Ca to Sr to Ba. Each step adds a new principal shell. That one idea explains a lot of the trends.

Group order: $$\text{Mg} \rightarrow \text{Ca} \rightarrow \text{Sr} \rightarrow \text{Ba}$$

**Check statement 1, ionic radius**

More shells means a larger ion, even after losing two outer electrons. So the radius of $\text{M}^{2+}$ increases down the group.

Trend: $$r(\text{Mg}^{2+}) < r(\text{Ca}^{2+}) < r(\text{Sr}^{2+}) < r(\text{Ba}^{2+})$$

**Check statement 2, screening**

Screening (shielding) is the repulsion by inner electrons that reduces the pull of the nucleus on the outer electrons. With more filled inner shells, screening increases.

Idea: $$\text{more inner shells} \rightarrow \text{greater screening}$$

**Check statement 3, hydroxide solubility**

This is a classic Group 2 trend to memorise. Solubility of $\text{M(OH)}_2$ increases down the group. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is almost insoluble, while $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble.

**Combine the three**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all increase from magnesium to barium, the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3 together.

options.A: Correct. All three increase. Ionic radius increases because of extra electron shells, screening increases because of more inner electrons, and solubility of $\text{M(OH)}_2$ increases down Group 2 from sparingly soluble $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ to soluble $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out statement 3. Many students remember size and shielding but forget or reverse the hydroxide solubility trend.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1. Ionic radius of $\text{M}^{2+}$ clearly increases down the group as new shells are added.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. It misses two correct trends. Both increased screening and increased hydroxide solubility are well established Group 2 trends.
